label: Edison's phonograph
detail: Edison's tinfoil phonograph is traditionally dated to 12 August 1877, though the Library of Congress notes it was probably built several months later, with the patent filed on 24 December 1877 (date disputed).

label: Savoy Theatre opens under electric light
detail: London's Savoy opens as the first public building lit entirely by electricity, with about 1,200 Swan lamps fed by a 120-horsepower generator.

label: The Savoy's stage goes electric
detail: The stage, kept on gas because the first generator was too small, switches to electric light, and Richard D'Oyly Carte breaks a lit bulb onstage to prove it is safe.

label: Berliner patents the gramophone
detail: Emile Berliner patents the flat-disc gramophone, the format that eventually displaced Edison's cylinders.

label: Fessenden's radio demonstration
detail: Reginald Fessenden demonstrates radio at Brant Rock, Massachusetts; his famous Christmas Eve 1906 broadcast is disputed and traces to a letter he wrote in 1932 (date disputed).

label: Magnavox loudspeaker demonstrated
detail: Jensen and Pridham's moving-coil Magnavox speaker is demonstrated publicly in Golden Gate Park, San Francisco, carrying music and a speech by the governor.

label: The theremin
detail: Leon Theremin's electronic instrument is usually dated to 1920, though the Moog Foundation's timeline lists it as Russia, 1924 (date disputed).

label: KDKA starts scheduled broadcasting
detail: Westinghouse's KDKA in East Pittsburgh reads out election returns at 100 watts, a pioneer of commercial broadcasting, though other stations claim to be older.

label: Musique concrète in Paris
detail: Pierre Schaeffer and colleagues at French radio's Studio d'Essai develop music assembled from recorded sound on tape.

label: Hanley Sound founded
detail: Bill Hanley, later known as the Father of Festival Sound and credited with moving the mixing desk out front, founds Hanley Sound in Medford, Massachusetts.

label: A sound clash at Forrester's Hall
detail: Prince Buster breaks Duke Reid's stylus at a late-1957 clash in Kingston. Jamaican sound systems date from the 1940s or the late 1940s (date disputed), and by the mid-1950s they were more popular than live bands at parties.

label: Poème électronique plays through 400 speakers
detail: Edgard Varèse's piece plays through 400 loudspeakers at the Brussels World's Fair, an early multi-speaker spatial sound installation.

label: King Tubby's Hometown Hi-Fi
detail: Osbourne Ruddock, King Tubby, founds Hometown Hi-Fi, the first sound system to bring reverb to the general public.

label: Caribbean carnival at St Pancras
detail: Claudia Jones organizes the first Caribbean carnival in London, indoors at St Pancras Town Hall. Rhaune Laslett starts the Notting Hill street festival in 1966, and static sound systems arrive in the 1970s.

label: Moog's modular synthesizer
detail: Robert Moog's transistorized, voltage-controlled synthesizer, programmed with patch cords, appears in the US, with Don Buchla's 100 series developing in parallel.

label: Joshua Light Show at the Fillmore East
detail: Joshua White's liquid light show becomes the house show at Bill Graham's Fillmore East, running until 1970.

label: Hanley's Woodstock rig
detail: Hanley Sound covers more than 400,000 people at Woodstock with what was described as one of the most expensive, elaborate and powerful sound systems ever built.

label: The Loft's first party
detail: David Mancuso's first Love Saves the Day party at his Broadway home, for about 100 people on an audiophile sound system engineered by Alex Rosner.

label: King Tubby makes dub
detail: In his front room at 18 Dromilly Avenue, Kingston, King Tubby makes dub on a used MCI desk by stripping out vocals, adding delay and reverb and sweeping the high-pass filter.

label: Technics SL-1200 launches
detail: The SL-1200 arrives as a hi-fi direct-drive turntable; its DJ career comes later.

label: Wall of Sound's rough debut
detail: A preliminary Grateful Dead Wall of Sound debuts at Stanford's Maples Pavilion, and every tweeter blows during the first song.

label: Pacha Ibiza opens
detail: Ricardo Urgell opens Pacha Ibiza.

label: Kool Herc's Sedgwick Avenue party
detail: DJ Kool Herc's back-to-school party in the Bronx becomes the conventional birthday of hip-hop, a date Rolling Stone frames as part history and part mystery.

label: The full Wall of Sound tours
detail: The Wall of Sound, about 75 tons of speakers in six separate systems, opens its tour at the Cow Palace; it is retired after Winterland in October 1974 as costs spiral.

label: New York lets private parties continue
detail: A Department of Consumer Affairs ruling lets private, alcohol-free parties continue, which benefits the Paradise Garage and other private clubs that run past bar hours.

label: The Mothership lands
detail: Parliament-Funkadelic's aluminum Mothership starts delivering Dr. Funkenstein to the stage, used at the end of concerts until 1981.

label: The Warehouse opens in Chicago
detail: Robert Williams's members-only Warehouse opens at 206 South Jefferson Street with a Richard Long sound system, and Frankie Knuckles becomes resident in March on Larry Levan's recommendation. In New York, the Paradise Garage holds construction parties during its renovation.

label: Paradise Garage officially opens
detail: After construction parties during its renovation, the members-only Paradise Garage at 84 King Street officially opens. It serves no alcohol so it can run until noon, and its sound is designed by Richard Long with Larry Levan.

label: SL-1200MK2 built for discos
detail: Technics releases the MK2, with a vertical pitch fader, which it calls the first turntable developed specifically for discos.

label: Disco Demolition
detail: A crate of disco records is blown up at Chicago's Comiskey Park; fans riot, 39 people are arrested and the second game is forfeited. Many records brought were by Black artists and were not disco.

label: Roland TR-808
detail: Roland releases the TR-808 drum machine, a flop new that became a core instrument of house and techno second-hand.

label: Pink Floyd's The Wall premieres
detail: The Wall opens at the LA Memorial Sports Arena with a 160-foot wall of 420 cardboard bricks built and torn down each night, and opening pyro sets a curtain on fire.

label: Roland TB-303
detail: Roland launches the TB-303 bass synthesizer; about 10,000 are sold before it is discontinued in under two years.

label: Hot Mix 5 on WBMX
detail: Chicago's WBMX starts broadcasting the Hot Mix 5's live DJ mixes, which reach a reported million listeners a week.

label: Vari-Lite debuts with Genesis
detail: The first Vari-Lite moving lights premiere at a Barcelona bullring on the opening night of Genesis' Abacab tour.

label: The Haçienda opens
detail: Factory Records' Manchester club opens; New Order's Peter Hook later said it lost up to 18 million pounds.

label: Alfredo at Amnesia
detail: Alfredo Fiorito first plays Amnesia, then an outdoor terrace club on Ibiza, where his eclectic "Balearic beat" sets take shape.

label: Jesse Saunders' "On and On"
detail: Jesse Saunders and Vince Lawrence's "On and On" uses a TR-808, a Korg Poly-61 and a TB-303. Its title as the first house record is contested by other Chicago and New York claims.

label: JumboTron at Expo '85
detail: Sony's JumboTron debuts in Tsukuba, Japan, with about 450,000 pixels of cathode-ray tube, years before full-color LED screens were possible.

label: DMX512 created
detail: USITT creates DMX512, the 512-channel lighting control standard now maintained by ESTA as ANSI E1.11.

label: Four London DJs in Ibiza
detail: Danny Rampling, Nicky Holloway, Johnny Walker and Paul Oakenfold hear Alfredo at Amnesia; back in London, Shoom, Future, Spectrum and The Trip follow.

label: Trax releases "Acid Tracks"
detail: Phuture's "Acid Tracks", which Ron Hardy had already broken at Chicago's Music Box from a tape, is released by Trax.

label: Belgian new beat
detail: New beat emerges in Belgium; the story of a 45 played at 33 rpm with the pitch at +8 credits different DJs and clubs.

label: "Strings of Life"
detail: Derrick May's "Strings of Life" is released in Detroit.

label: Paradise Garage closes
detail: The NYC LGBT Historic Sites Project gives 26 September 1987 as the closing date; the lease ended on 1 October 1987 (date disputed).

label: Second Summer of Love
detail: UK acid house explodes from clubs like Shoom to orbital raves around the M25, peaking in 1989.

label: Techno gets its name
detail: The UK compilation Techno! The New Dance Sound of Detroit, working title The House Sound of Detroit, fixes the genre's name; compiler Neil Rushton says the four of them chose it together.

label: The tabloids turn on acid house
detail: A week after calling acid house "cool and groovy" on 12 October, tabloid coverage switches to "Evils of Ecstasy".

label: Underground Resistance forms
detail: "Mad" Mike Banks and Jeff Mills form Underground Resistance in Detroit, with anonymity against the superstar-DJ model.

label: The first Love Parade
detail: Dr. Motte and Danielle de Picciotto start the Love Parade in West Berlin with about 150 people; it tops a million attendees a year from 1997 to 2000.

label: UK raises fines for unlicensed parties
detail: The Entertainments (Increased Penalties) Act raises fines for unlicensed parties from 2,000 to 20,000 pounds, with up to six months in prison.

label: Denon DN-2000F unveiled
detail: Denon shows its rack-mounted dual CD controller at NAMM, reaching booths in 1992; Wikipedia dates a Denon dual-deck to 1993, possibly a different model (date disputed).

label: Tresor opens
detail: Dimitri Hegemann opens Tresor in the vaults of the former Wertheim department store in Berlin; Tresor Records follows in October and releases Detroit artists.

label: Ministry of Sound opens
detail: Inspired by the Paradise Garage, the London club opens in a disused bus garage, spending 500,000 pounds each on sound and soundproofing.

label: L-Acoustics V-DOSC
detail: L-Acoustics introduces the V-DOSC line array, built on what it calls Wavefront Sculpture Technology.

label: U2's Zoo TV tour begins
detail: Zoo TV runs 157 shows synced almost entirely to pre-programmed video and audio, at 125,000 dollars a day.

label: Castlemorton Common
detail: A week-long free party begins with an estimated 20,000 to 40,000 people and sound systems including Spiral Tribe; it is usually credited with prompting the 1994 Act.

label: Pioneer CDJ-500
detail: Pioneer releases what it calls the first flat-top CD DJ player, with live cue, looping and master tempo.

label: Criminal Justice and Public Order Act
detail: The UK act, whose section 63 targets outdoor gatherings with music of "repetitive beats", receives Royal Assent.

label: U2 PopMart's LED screen
detail: U2's PopMart tour carries an LED screen about 150 to 170 feet wide, built from 150,000 pixels by SACO Technologies.

label: Insomniac's first EDC
detail: Insomniac's Electric Daisy Carnival debuts at the Shrine Expo Hall in Los Angeles.

label: The first Boom Festival
detail: Boom is first held in Portugal; it becomes biennial from 1998 and the flagship of psytrance.

label: First Ultra Music Festival
detail: Ultra debuts on Miami Beach for about 10,000 people.

label: Fabric opens
detail: London's Fabric opens with three rooms of independent sound and a bodysonic floor of 400 bass transducers.

label: Detroit Electronic Music Festival
detail: The free festival opens at Hart Plaza; Paxahau has produced it as Movement since 2006.

label: FWD>> starts
detail: FWD>>, the first night dedicated to dubstep, is founded at the Velvet Rooms and then moves to Plastic People in Shoreditch.

label: Ableton Live 1.0
detail: Ableton releases Live, whose warping makes beat-matched hybrid laptop sets possible.

label: The Station nightclub fire
detail: Pyrotechnic gerbs ignite acoustic foam at a Rhode Island club, killing 100 people and reshaping nightclub sprinkler and pyro rules.

label: RAVE Act becomes law
detail: The Illicit Drug Anti-Proliferation Act extends the US crack house statute to temporary events, chilling on-site harm reduction.

label: Berghain opens
detail: Berghain opens in a former Berlin power plant; its first Funktion-One stack goes in the next year.

label: Form 696
detail: London's Metropolitan Police create Form 696, a club risk-assessment form later used to shut grime events.

label: First Tomorrowland
detail: Tomorrowland debuts in Boom, Belgium, for about 10,000 people.

label: Mixed In Key released
detail: Key-detection software Mixed In Key is first released and makes harmonic mixing mainstream.

label: Daft Punk's pyramid
detail: Daft Punk debut their LED pyramid, built from off-the-shelf parts, in Coachella's Sahara Tent, sparking an arms race in live-show technology.

label: Laser injuries near Moscow
detail: Lasers meant for the sky hit the crowd in tents at a rain-hit festival in Kirzhach; Reuters reported 29 people treated, ILDA puts it at 35.

label: CDJ-2000, PRO DJ LINK and rekordbox
detail: Pioneer announces the CDJ-2000, which plays from USB, links up to four players over Ethernet and comes with rekordbox, so DJs can arrive with only a USB stick.

label: deadmau5 unveils the Cube
detail: deadmau5 debuts his first LED Cube at Coachella.

label: Love Parade disaster
detail: Twenty-one people die and 652 are injured in a crowd crush at a single entrance ramp in Duisburg; the Love Parade is canceled for good.

label: Amon Tobin's ISAM premieres
detail: ISAM Live premieres at MUTEK in Montreal, projection-mapped onto a stack of cubes by a custom TouchDesigner application.

label: Indiana State Fair stage collapse
detail: A gust of about 59 mph brings down a stage roof rated for 68 mph before a Sugarland concert, killing seven.

label: Pukkelpop storm
detail: A sudden storm brings down a stage, a tent and screens at the Belgian festival, which is canceled; five deaths is the commonly cited toll, unverified from an official source.

label: Event Safety Alliance debuts
detail: Formed in response to Indiana and led by Jim Digby, the ESA debuts at the Indiana Statehouse, modeled on the UK's Purple Guide.

label: The "Tupac hologram"
detail: Coachella's Tupac performance uses Pepper's ghost, a flat image reflected off angled film, not a true hologram.

label: "We all hit play"
detail: deadmau5 posts that he just selects tracks and hits a spacebar, reported on 25 June 2012 and starting the genre's longest argument.

label: Live Nation and Insomniac
detail: Pasquale Rotella announces a "creative partnership" with Live Nation, terms undisclosed; it is usually described as a 50% stake.

label: Pioneer sells its DJ business to KKR
detail: Pioneer agrees to sell 86% of its DJ business to KKR for about 59 billion yen, creating Pioneer DJ Corporation.

label: The Show Must Go On
detail: Powerful Thinking estimates UK festivals emit about 100,000 metric tons of CO2 equivalent a year, with audience travel up to 80%.

label: Dolby Atmos at Ministry of Sound
detail: The Box gets an object-based Dolby Atmos system of more than 60 speakers on 22 channels, playing specially prepared tracks.

label: The Loop's first UK drug checking
detail: The Loop runs the UK's first event-based drug checking at Secret Garden Party and Kendal Calling.

label: SFX files for bankruptcy
detail: SFX Entertainment files for Chapter 11 with about $300 million of debt swapped for equity, and ousts its founder, Robert F.X. Sillerman.

label: Drones at the Super Bowl
detail: Intel's 300 Shooting Star drones appear in the halftime show, filmed days earlier because of flight restrictions around the stadium.

label: CDJs talk to ShowKontrol
detail: CDJs can send real-time waveforms and track data over PRO DJ LINK to ShowKontrol, which generates timecode from whatever is playing.

label: Pioneer DJ becomes AlphaTheta
detail: Pioneer DJ Corporation renames itself AlphaTheta Corporation; Noritsu buys it later in 2020.

label: CDJ-3000 announced
detail: Pioneer DJ announces the CDJ-3000, with a 9-inch touchscreen, eight hot cues, gigabit link for six players and no disc drive.

label: #RedAlertRESTART
detail: More than 1,500 US venues, landmarks and homes are lit red for #WeMakeEvents, calling for aid to small businesses and freelance 1099 workers.

label: Last Night a DJ Took a Flight
detail: Clean Scene estimates the top 1,000 DJs took more than 51,000 flights in 2019, producing about 35,000 metric tons of CO2.

label: Astroworld crowd crush
detail: Ten people die of compression asphyxia at the Houston festival; about half an hour passes between the mass-casualty declaration and the end of the show.

label: WHO safe listening standard
detail: The World Health Organization recommends no more than 100 dB LAeq over 15 minutes at venues and events.

label: Serato adds real-time stems
detail: Serato DJ Pro and Lite 3.0 add four real-time stems, part of stem separation going mainstream.

label: FDA Laser Notice 56
detail: FDA says it will not enforce certain US laser requirements for products meeting IEC 60825-1 Edition 3; show variances are unaffected.

label: Sphere opens
detail: The 2.3 billion dollar Las Vegas venue opens with U2, wrapping the audience in a 16K by 16K LED screen.

label: Berlin techno on a heritage list
detail: "Techno culture in Berlin" enters Germany's National Inventory of Intangible Cultural Heritage, often misreported as UNESCO's international list.

label: UK drug checking licensed
detail: The Loop receives the first Home Office license for on-site drug checking after a 2023 licensing requirement halted it.

label: Twitch DJ Program announced
detail: Twitch announces a label-licensed program for live DJ streaming; the DJ category launches on 8 August 2024.

label: ACT 1.5 in Bristol
detail: Massive Attack play a battery-powered, plant-based, rail-first show for more than 32,000 people; the Tyndall Centre reports power emissions cut 81-98% against a modeled typical concert.

label: Anyma at Sphere
detail: Anyma's The End of Genesys opens as the first electronic music residency at Sphere, running into March 2025.

label: Club Pulse fire, Kočani
detail: Stage pyrotechnics ignite a flammable ceiling at a North Macedonian club, killing at least 59.

label: UK SORA for drones
detail: The UK Civil Aviation Authority starts assessing Specific-category drone authorizations, including swarms and flights near crowds, under the UK SORA method.

label: 10,518 drones in Vietnam
detail: Guinness recognizes 10,518 drones from DAMODA as the largest drone light show by number flying at once; later public shows are canceled.

label: US all-in ticket pricing
detail: The FTC rule takes effect requiring live-event ticket sellers to show the total price, including mandatory fees, wherever a price is shown.

label: Tomorrowland mainstage burns
detail: The Orbyz mainstage burns during a final pyro rehearsal less than 48 hours before opening; a smaller replacement, partly built from Metallica's touring rig, goes up within roughly 24 to 48 hours, depending on the source.

label: Queensland bans pill testing
detail: Queensland, which closed its sites in April 2025, becomes the first Australian state to ban pill testing.

label: CDJ-3000X announced
detail: AlphaTheta announces the CDJ-3000X with Wi-Fi, cloud and streaming playback and no SD slot.

label: NFPA 1126 and 160, 2026 editions
detail: The 2026 NFPA 1126 requires every proximate pyro operator to be a pyrotechnic professional, and NFPA 160 makes flame operators responsible for safe removal timing.

label: Le Constellation fire, Crans-Montana
detail: A New Year's fire at a Swiss bar kills 40; the preliminary cause is sparklers on champagne bottles held too close to the ceiling.

label: NSW funds continued festival drug checking
detail: New South Wales ends its festival trial after testing more than 1,500 samples and commits A$4.3 million to continue testing at up to 15 festivals a year; it is funded continuation, not legislation.

label: A $15.1 billion business
detail: The IMS Business Report values the global electronic music industry at a record $15.1 billion for 2025, up 7%.

label: inMusic agrees to buy Native Instruments
detail: inMusic, owner of Denon DJ and Rane, agrees to buy Traktor's maker after it entered preliminary insolvency; completion was not confirmed as of June 2026.

label: AlphaTheta acquires DJ Monitor technology
detail: AlphaTheta buys DJ Monitor's technology and assets to make KUVO a hub for club performance data for rights organizations.

label: A new Mothership lands
detail: A lighter third version of Parliament-Funkadelic's Mothership lands at ESSENCE Fest in New Orleans.

label: Event Safety Alliance at 15
detail: The ESA marks 15 years since Indiana and is developing a second Event Safety Guide and an OSHA 10 course for live events.

label: rekordbox adds official SoundSwitch support
detail: rekordbox and PRO DJ LINK Bridge add official SoundSwitch lighting support, replacing an older Ableton Link tempo-sync integration.
